skill.name: swiftui-expert-skill
skill.description: Guides SwiftUI development, reviews, and refactors with modern state management, view composition, performance, Swift concurrency, and Liquid Glass guidance.
skill.summary: Guides SwiftUI feature work, reviews, and refactors with modern iOS patterns.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: I reviewed SKILL.md and found the static alerts are false positives from Markdown formatting, SwiftUI terms, and source attribution. No executable command path, data exfiltration behavior, prompt injection attempt, or unsafe network instruction was found.

static_findings.snippet: - Check property wrapper usage against the selection guide (see `references/state-management.md`)
- Verify view composition follows extraction rules (see `references/view-structure.md`)
- Verify list patterns use stable identity (see `references/list-patterns.md`)
- Inspect Liquid Glass usage for correctness and consistency (see `references/liquid-glass.md`)
- Audit state management for correct wrapper selection (prefer `@Observable` over `ObservableObject`
- Replace deprecated APIs with modern equivalents (see `references/modern-apis.md`)
- Extract complex views into separate subviews (see `references/view-structure.md`)
- Refactor hot paths to minimize redundant state updates (see `references/performance-patterns.md`)
- Suggest image downsampling when `UIImage(data:)` is used (as optional optimization, see `reference
- Design data flow first: identify owned vs injected state (see `references/state-management.md`)
- Use modern APIs (no deprecated modifiers or patterns, see `references/modern-apis.md`)
- Use `@Observable` for shared state (with `@MainActor` if not using default actor isolation)
- Structure views for optimal diffing (extract subviews early, keep views small, see `references/vie
- Separate business logic into testable models (see `references/layout-best-practices.md`)
- Apply glass effects after layout/appearance modifiers (see `references/liquid-glass.md`)
- Gate iOS 26+ features with `#available` and provide fallbacks
- **Mark `@Observable` classes with `@MainActor`** unless using default actor isolation
- **Never declare passed values as `@State` or `@StateObject`** (they only accept initial values)
- `@Binding` only when child needs to **modify** parent state
- Use `let` for read-only values; `var` + `.onChange()` for reactive reads
- Nested `ObservableObject` doesn't work (pass nested objects directly); `@Observable` handles nesti
- Use `.sheet(item:)` instead of `.sheet(isPresented:)` for model-based content
- Sheets should own their actions and call `dismiss()` internally
- Use `ScrollViewReader` for programmatic scrolling with stable IDs
- Use modern Text formatting (`.format` parameters, not `String(format:)`)
- Use `.task` modifier for automatic cancellation of async work
- Keep view `body` simple and pure (no side effects or complex logic)
- Use `@ViewBuilder` functions only for small, simple sections
- Prefer `@ViewBuilder let content: Content` over closure-based content properties
- Avoid redundant state updates in `onReceive`, `onChange`, scroll handlers
- Use stable identity for `ForEach` (never `.indices` for dynamic content)
- Ensure constant number of views per `ForEach` element
- Avoid inline filtering in `ForEach` (prefilter and cache)
- Suggest image downsampling when `UIImage(data:)` is encountered (as optional optimization)
- Use `Self._printChanges()` to debug unexpected view updates
- Use native `glassEffect`, `GlassEffectContainer`, and glass button styles
- Apply `.glassEffect()` after layout and visual modifiers
| `@State` | Internal view state (must be `private`), or owned `@Observable` class |
| `onChange(of:) { value in }` | `onChange(of:) { old, new in }` or `onChange(of:) { }` |
- [ ] Using `@Observable` instead of `ObservableObject` for new code
- [ ] Passed values NOT declared as `@State` or `@StateObject`
- [ ] `@Binding` only where child modifies parent state
- [ ] Nested `ObservableObject` avoided (or passed directly to child views)
- [ ] Using `ScrollViewReader` with stable IDs for programmatic scrolling
- [ ] Container views use `@ViewBuilder let content: Content`
- [ ] View `body` kept simple and pure (no side effects)
- `references/view-structure.md` - View composition, extraction, and container patterns
- `references/list-patterns.md` - ForEach identity, stability, and list best practices
- `references/layout-best-practices.md` - Layout patterns, context-agnostic views, and testability
- `references/modern-apis.md` - Modern API usage and deprecated replacements
- `references/text-formatting.md` - Modern text formatting and string operations
- We emphasize thread safety with `@MainActor` and `@Observable`

content.value_statement: SwiftUI teams need current guidance for state, layout, performance, and modern APIs. This skill turns reviews and feature requests into practical SwiftUI recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Reviews SwiftUI state management and property wrapper choices.
Recommends modern replacements for deprecated SwiftUI APIs.
Guides view extraction, composition, and performance checks.
Checks list identity, sheets, navigation, text formatting, and scroll patterns.
Provides Liquid Glass guidance with availability gates and fallbacks.
Helps plan new SwiftUI features around ownership and data flow.
limitations: It provides guidance and examples, but it does not run Xcode builds.
It focuses on SwiftUI and iOS patterns, not full UIKit architecture.
Some API advice depends on the target SDK and deployment version.
Liquid Glass guidance applies only when the user requests iOS 26 or newer design.

use_cases.title: Plan a New SwiftUI Feature
use_cases.description: Define state ownership, data flow, navigation, and view boundaries before implementation.

use_cases.title: Review a SwiftUI Pull Request
use_cases.description: Find incorrect property wrappers, deprecated APIs, unstable lists, and expensive view updates.

use_cases.title: Modernize Legacy Views
use_cases.description: Replace older SwiftUI patterns with current APIs while preserving behavior and compatibility.

prompt_templates.title: Review One View
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of a focused SwiftUI component.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this SwiftUI view for state management, modern APIs, and simple performance issues. Explain each recommendation clearly.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor a Screen
prompt_templates.scenario: Improve an existing screen without changing product behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this SwiftUI screen plan. Focus on view extraction, stable identity, navigation, and testable business logic.

prompt_templates.title: Plan Feature Architecture
prompt_templates.scenario: Design a new SwiftUI feature before writing code.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan this SwiftUI feature. Identify owned state, injected dependencies, bindings, async tasks, and availability checks.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Modernization Risk
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review before migrating a larger SwiftUI area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this SwiftUI module for deprecated APIs, performance hot paths, concurrency risks, and optional Liquid Glass adoption.

output_examples.input: Review a list screen that filters items inside the list loop and uses index-based identity.
output_examples.output: The skill would flag unstable identity, recommend prefiltered data, and suggest stable model identifiers for updates.

output_examples.input: Plan a detail screen that edits shared model data and presents a modal editor.
output_examples.output: The skill would separate owned state from injected models, choose bindings carefully, and recommend model-based sheet presentation.

output_examples.input: Modernize a SwiftUI card that uses older color and corner APIs.
output_examples.output: The skill would recommend current style APIs, preserve layout behavior, and gate newer visual effects behind availability checks.

best_practices: Share the target iOS version and SDK before asking for API guidance.
Provide complete view context when asking for state management advice.
Ask for behavior-preserving changes when refactoring production views.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to choose a full architecture without product context.
Do not apply Liquid Glass styling unless the platform target supports it.
Do not accept performance advice without checking behavior in Instruments or Xcode.

faq.question: Does this skill write SwiftUI code?
faq.answer: Yes. It can draft SwiftUI views, refactors, and review comments based on the provided context.

faq.question: Can it replace Xcode warnings or compiler checks?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance, but build errors and diagnostics must be verified in Xcode.

faq.question: Does it require a specific architecture?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on state ownership, testability, and SwiftUI patterns without enforcing one architecture.

faq.question: Can it help with older iOS targets?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the deployment target so it can suggest compatible APIs and fallbacks.

faq.question: Does it support Liquid Glass guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers Liquid Glass patterns when the user explicitly requests iOS 26 or newer styling.

faq.question: Is it useful for code review?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes checklist-style guidance for state, lists, navigation, layout, and performance.
